items.q: What is the slope of the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \sin x</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \pi</annotation></semantics></math>?

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin \pi</annotation></semantics></math>, the height. The slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos \pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

The sign: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos \pi = -1</annotation></semantics></math>, and the graph is falling as it crosses <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which is an equation of the line tangent to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \sin x</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>?

For <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le x \le 2\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, where is the line tangent to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \sin x</annotation></semantics></math> level?

For <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le x \le 2\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, at which <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> is the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \sin x</annotation></semantics></math> falling most steeply?
Evaluate L1.

mistakes.why: Substituting <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h = 0</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>0</mn><mn>0</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{0}{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is not 0. Read L1 as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(2)</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = e^x</annotation></semantics></math>.

The power rule does not apply to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^x</annotation></semantics></math>. The derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^x</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^x</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(2) = e^2</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Evaluate L2.

mistakes.why: The derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\sin x</annotation></semantics></math>: keep the minus sign.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos \frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, the value subtracted in the numerator. The limit is the slope, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\sin \frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Evaluate L3.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>0</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\ln 1}{0}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>0</mn><mn>0</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{0}{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, not 0. Since <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln 1 = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, L3 is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>h</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{h \to 0} \frac{\ln(1 + h) - \ln 1}{h}</annotation></semantics></math>, the derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln x</annotation></semantics></math> at 1.

items.q: Evaluate L4.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin \frac{\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>, the height. L4 is the slope of sine there, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos \frac{\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>.

L4 is the derivative of sine, which is cosine with no sign change: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos \frac{\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Differentiate the combination <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\sin x - 2\cos x</annotation></semantics></math> term by term.

mistakes.why: The derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\sin x</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2\cos x</annotation></semantics></math> becomes <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2(-\sin x) = +2\sin x</annotation></semantics></math>.

The derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+\cos x</annotation></semantics></math>; only cosine picks up a minus sign.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(x)</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = 4e^x - \ln x</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The power rule needs a fixed exponent; in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^x</annotation></semantics></math> the variable is the exponent. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dx}\left( e^x \right) = e^x</annotation></semantics></math>.

The minus sign stays: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dx}(-\ln x) = -\frac{1}{x}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln x</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{x}</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln x</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = x^2 + 5\ln x</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln x</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{x}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\ln x</annotation></semantics></math> becomes <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{5}{x}</annotation></semantics></math>.

Keep the constant factor: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dx}(5\ln x) = 5 \cdot \frac{1}{x}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: What is the slope of the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = e^x</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \ln 3</annotation></semantics></math>?

mistakes.why: That is the input. The slope of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^x</annotation></semantics></math> equals its height: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{\ln 3} = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

The slope of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^x</annotation></semantics></math> is 1 only at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>. At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \ln 3</annotation></semantics></math> it is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{\ln 3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which is an equation of the line tangent to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \ln x</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = e</annotation></semantics></math>?

What is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dx}(\cos x)</annotation></semantics></math>?

items.q: Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(x) = f(x)g(x)</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h'(1)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(1)g'(1) = 2 \cdot 4</annotation></semantics></math>, the product of the derivatives. That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(1) = f(1)g(1)</annotation></semantics></math>, a value. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(1) = -1</annotation></semantics></math>, so the second term is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-1)(4) = -4</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6 - 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k(x) = x^2 f(x)</annotation></semantics></math>. mistakes.why: That multiplies the derivatives, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x \cdot f'(x) = 6(-2)</annotation></semantics></math>. Use <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x\,f(x) + x^2 f'(x)</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is only the first term, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2(3)f(3)</annotation></semantics></math>. Add <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 f'(x) = 9(-2)</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k(3) = 9 \cdot 4</annotation></semantics></math>, a value, not a slope.

items.q: Which is an equation of the line tangent to the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(x) = f(x)g(x)</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>?

Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q'(0)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^0 \cdot g'(0)</annotation></semantics></math>, the product of the two derivatives. Add <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^0 g'(0) = -1</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u'(1)</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u(x) = f(x)g(x)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(1)g'(1) = (2)(-1)</annotation></semantics></math>. Use <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(4)g(4) + f(4)g'(4)</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u(4) = 3 \cdot 4</annotation></semantics></math>, the value.

items.q: What is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u'(2)</annotation></semantics></math>?

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math>, using the slopes of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> just to the left of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-7</annotation></semantics></math>, using the slopes of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> just to the right of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-4</annotation></semantics></math>, the average of the two one-sided slopes of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(x) = x\,g(x)</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v'(1)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 \cdot g'(1)</annotation></semantics></math>, the product of the derivatives of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>. That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(1) = 1 \cdot g(1)</annotation></semantics></math>, or the first term alone.

items.q: Use the product rule to differentiate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 \sin x</annotation></semantics></math>, a power of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> times a sine.

options: The slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sec</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec^2 x = \frac{1}{\cos^2 x}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 < \cos^2 x \le 1</annotation></semantics></math> there.
